The garden owns one mount, logseq-encode-garden. Its bucket is public, and its DVC backups sit in the same bucket under dvc/, so they are public too. That's why Asset/mise/Task/add refuses WAV, AIFF and FLAC files. Logseq/Entity/Asset/B2

A second mount with its own private bucket and DVC remote, declared without public, would hold recordings. mise run site:build already stops when a page links into a mount without public, so a recording can't be published by accident. Asset/Mount The asset:* tasks keep files in the one mount the garden owns, so they would need to take a mount name.

Sets carry absolute paths from your home folder. Each sample reference holds a RelativePath and an absolute Path, such as /Users/<user>/Music/Ableton/User Library/Samples/Recorded/… in LPP-Seq. As XML in git those paths become plain text in a public repository. The identity guard in lefthook.yml scans the working file, which is gzip, so it would likely miss them. The two GitP templates in the public bucket carry such paths today.

Collect All and Save copies samples into the project folder (Ableton/Live/UG/05 Managing Files and Sets/07 Collecting External Files), and the absolute Path then points inside the project, which still sits in your home folder. Whether Live opens a Set whose clean filter rewrote those paths is untested.

A static site can't check who is reading, so a login needs a small service. It checks the reader and returns a short-lived download link to a file in the private bucket. B2's b2_get_download_authorization issues a token limited to a file-name prefix and a duration. The site build would then link a private-mount file to that service instead of stopping. A shop is the same service with a payment step before the link.

DVC keeps a copy in .dvc/cache of every file the current commit references, 2.2 GB in this garden today. dvc gc --workspace keeps every file the workspace still references, so it never frees a finished project. dvc gc
Offloading a project needs a small task: check with dvc status --cloud that B2 has it, then delete its working files and their cache entries. Asset/mise/Task/fetch brings a file back on demand.
With Sets in git, the Set stays on the Mac and only its Samples folder is offloaded.

A drive copy can be a second DVC remote. dvc remote add --local drive /Volumes/<drive>/dvc keeps the drive's path in .dvc/config.local, outside git, and dvc push -r drive copies the objects B2 holds. dvc remote add

Must every sample reference in a Set hold an absolute path containing my username? It seems like Ableton has a feature called Collect All and Save. I need to be able to move Ableton Sets, or maybe Ableton projects, to different drives.
AI/Response No, Live doesn't need the absolute path to find a file, but it writes one anyway.

Each file reference in a Set's XML holds a relative path and an absolute one. In the LPP-Seq template, for example, a recording appears as <RelativePathType Value="6" />, <RelativePath Value="Samples/Recorded/mf1 0001 [2026-10-24 163409]-3.aif" /> and <Path Value="~/Music/Ableton/User Library/Samples/Recorded/mf1 0001 [2026-10-24 163409]-3.aif" />, with the home folder shortened to ~ here. Even its project-relative references carry an absolute Path beside the relative one.
AI/Response No, Live doesn't need the absolute path to find a file, but it writes one anyway.
Collect All and Save copies the files a Set uses into its Project folder, so the relative paths point inside the Project. That is what lets a Project move to another drive and still open.
AI/Response No, Live doesn't need the absolute path to find a file, but it writes one anyway.

So moving between drives works through the relative paths, but every save writes the absolute path again, username included. A clean filter could rewrite each Path value, for example to ~, before git stores the XML. Whether Live then opens the Set without asking to locate files needs testing on a copy.

Plan for keeping whole Live projects in this garden under assets/Ableton/Project/, carrying out the recommendation on Ableton/Live/Idea/Store-Ableton-in-the-Garden. Sets and presets go in git as XML through a clean/smudge filter. Each project's Samples/ folder goes to a new private Backblaze/B2 bucket, logseq-encode-garden-private, through dvc. Rendered MP3s and images stay asset pages in the public bucket, logseq-encode-garden, as Logseq/Entity/Asset/B2 describes.

Git, through the ableton filter, stored as XML: .als Sets, .alc clips, .adg rack presets and .adv device presets. All four are gzip-compressed XML; one factory .adv uses Live's binary format, and gzip -dcf passes it through unchanged.
Git, as is: .agr, .ask and .xmp files. Some .agr grooves are binary, so they stay out of the filter.
DVC, private bucket: the Samples/ folder of each project, as one directory output whose .dvc file names remote: private. Recordings on this Mac are .aif, so this covers every audio format.
DVC, public bucket: MP3s, PNGs and other published outputs, through the existing asset:* tasks and the logseq-encode-garden mount.
Ignored: Backup/ (git history replaces Live's timestamped copies), *.asd analysis files, which Live rebuilds, and the macOS Icon\r file.

A project documents one garden page, its owner, such as a session GitP/A/Session/26/11/06-Fri or a template GitP/A/Template/LPP-Seq. The folder name is the owner's page name written the way Logseq/Entity/Asset writes file names: ___ for each / and hyphens for spaces.
A Set file's name maps back to its Set page by turning ___ into /. The main Set is <owner>___Set.als; another Set in the same project adds a name, <owner>___Set___<Name>.als.

mise run ableton:set:import --als <file> --performance '<owner>' already writes <owner>/Set and its <owner>/Set/Track/... pages per Logseq/Entity/Ableton/Set. Its source:: property would hold the Set's path from the repository root, so a reader can open the file from the page.
A Set page names its file in source:: as text. A Markdown link to a git-tracked .als under assets/ would make Logseq/Entity/Proxy/Page/mise/Task/sync copy the gzip working file into gitpa.
Live saves only into the primary checkout. A linked worktree holds the Sets but no Samples/, so an agent can edit a Set's XML on a branch and the PR shows the diff.
Run on 2026-11-28 Sat in codekiln/making-music (private), tracked in making-music#1 Experiments for keeping Live projects in git and DVC.

making-music#2 Clean/smudge filter that swaps the home folder: on the LPP-Seq and Pattern A and B templates and two session Sets, clean then smudge gave back Live's XML unchanged. Clean twice changed nothing, two clones wrote the same .als, and a clone with another $HOME got that home folder in every path.
After clean, no username was left in the four Sets. Before clean they held it on 48, 0, 274 and 463 lines, all in FileRef/Path.
Seven saved versions of one session Set took 1.5 MB of git storage through the filter and 7.2 MB as Live's gzip files.

A plain git clone with the filter configured fails when the smudge script is a file in the same repository: git writes the Sets before the script. The filter commands have to live outside the repository, in the dotfiles gitconfig or a script installed by mise.

making-music#3 Pre-commit check for gzip and home-folder leaks in staged Sets: the check reads staged blobs and refuses gzip, non-XML, the current $HOME and the username, including the username as a folder name in a RelativePath.

A rule against every /Users/<name> path refused all four real Sets: each holds three paths from factory presets naming the home folders of people at Ableton. making-music#9 dropped that rule. CI runs as another user, so it sees a username only through a SET_LEAK_NAMES repository secret.

making-music#4 DVC Samples folder routed to a private B2 remote used the logseq-garden bucket as the private remote and logseq-encode-garden as the public one, each with its own key, under experiments/making-music/dvc/.
A stub Samples.dvc keeps remote: private through dvc add and a re-add. dvc add writes /Samples to the project's .gitignore, and the .als stays tracked. *.asd in .dvcignore keeps analysis files out.

With one key per bucket, a plain dvc push or dvc pull fails with a 403 on the other bucket. Every task names its .dvc targets and its remote. An untargeted dvc pull -r public still reads the private .dir object and fails.
dvc status -c reports a private object in sync when it is missing. dvc data status --not-in-remote --granular with -r private finds it.
B2 keeps a deleted object as a hidden version, so deleting from a bucket means deleting every version.
Create the B2 bucket logseq-encode-garden-private with private access, and an application key restricted to it. Store the key in 1Password and add a fnox profile for it beside assets in fnox.toml.

Add the remote to .dvc/config: ['remote "private"'], url = s3://logseq-encode-garden-private/dvc/, endpointurl = https://s3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com. Leave core.remote = garden; the 835 existing .dvc files rely on it.

Add a root .gitattributes: assets/Ableton/Project/**/*.als filter=ableton -merge, and the same line for .alc, .adg and .adv. -merge makes two branches that both changed a Set stop with a conflict, since a line merge can produce XML Live can't load.

Install the clean and smudge scripts from making-music experiments/2-home-swap-filter outside the repository, and define [filter "ableton"] to run them in the global gitconfig in codekiln/dotfiles chezmoi/dot_gitconfig, and add a mise task, ableton:filter:install, that sets the same two keys in one clone. Leave filter.ableton.required off, so the Publish workflow's clone, which has no filter, checks out plain XML.
Add a lefthook pre-commit check that every staged blob for those four extensions starts with <?xml. A clone without the filter would otherwise commit gzip.
Point the identity guard in lefthook.yml at the staged XML (git show :<path>). It reads the working file, which is gzip, so it misses the home-folder paths each <Path Value=...> holds.

Write ableton:project:add <owner>. It checks that the owner page exists, that the folder name matches it, and that every sample reference in each Set is relative to the project, which Collect All and Save does (Ableton/Live/UG/05 Managing Files and Sets/07 Collecting External Files). Then it writes the project .gitignore, writes a stub Samples.dvc holding path: Samples and remote: private, runs dvc add, and stages the Sets.

Write ableton:project:push, ableton:project:fetch and ableton:project:offload, running DVC with -r private under the private fnox profile. offload checks dvc data status --not-in-remote before deleting Samples/ and its cache entries; dvc status -c skips outputs routed to their own remote.

Add a check that every .dvc file under assets/Ableton/Project/ names remote: private, as a lefthook command and in the tasks' tests. A Samples.dvc without it goes to the public bucket on the next dvc push.
